fact: The head of Zambia's Presidential Delivery Unit announced on 17 July 2026 that the country's National AI Strategy was nearing completion, and the Ministry of Technology and Science referred to the forthcoming National AI Strategy; the article does not mention an earlier adopted strategy.

The Ministry of Technology and Science published the Zambia National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, titled 2024-2026 on its cover and 2025-2027 in its page headers, and announced its launch on 21 November 2024; the document carries no adoption date of its own, so the date is the launch announcement as proxied in the source page.

The strategy sets up a National AI Council with sector Technical Working Groups, makes Smart Zambia Institute the coordinator of AI implementation within government and the Ministry of Technology and Science the lead for adoption across the economy; the date is the strategy's publication date, as the document gives none of its own.

A COMESA Secretariat telecommunications officer said in Kigali on 3 August 2026 that Zambia has developed an AI strategy and is working on additional frameworks and initiatives to support implementation; he did not give an adoption date.

At a Lusaka consultation on 22-23 June 2026 the Ministry of Technology and Science's Permanent Secretary spoke of the country implementing its National AI Strategy, and UNESCO said the strategy expires at the end of 2026 and that Zambia is preparing to review and renew it.
The article describes the National AI Strategy 2024-2026 as Zambia's plan, with Finland to give technical assistance, per the Ministry of Technology and Science.

Research ICT Africa says Zambia's National AI Strategy was launched in November 2024 and calls for AI adoption across six areas including health, agriculture, education, mining, climate and public services.
The Ministry of Technology and Science launched the Artificial Intelligence Strategy in Lusaka, with Minister Felix Mutati presiding, supported by Finland and the Tony Blair Institute.
The document refers to Zambia's National AI Strategy (2024-2026) and says the Ministry of Technology and Science announced an AI Center of Excellence in September 2024 following its adoption.
